paras: The reported lynching of Anderson Bunch was the reported hanging, in July 1882, of a man near Paoli, Indiana, who was accused of helping the accused murderer of Martin H. Archer to escape. Wire dispatches from New Albany, which called him Bundy, said a mob hanged him at night and threw his body into Lost River, and the story ran in papers from Maine to Arizona. The local Paoli News, however, reported only that he had disappeared and that foul play was suspected.

In mid-July a Kentucky paper reported that Martin H. Archer had been murdered by Samuel Marley at Paoli. Later accounts placed the killing at West Baden Springs, near Paoli, and in French Lick township, and one syndicated paragraph described it as committed "in a most cowardly and brutal manner." Marley escaped, and the New Albany dispatch said he had lived with Bundy, whose "crime" was aiding that escape. One condensed dispatch alone said Bundy freed Marley "from prison."

According to the Paoli News, Anderson Bunch, who lived near the scene of the murder and was said to be friendly to Marley, left his home on the evening of Tuesday, July 11, to look after hogs running loose in the woods and did not return. Pistol shots were reported heard that evening near where he was last seen. Searchers combed the woods and dragged Lost River expecting to find his body.

The wire version, datelined New Albany on July 25, was more definite: Bundy had been hanged at night by a mob and his body thrown into Lost River. The National Associated Press report named him "J. Bundy" and placed the hanging at "Baden Springs," and the syndicated paragraph added that the mob hanged him to a tree.
No report of a recovered body, an inquest, arrests or prosecutions appears in the coverage. No paper stated the race of Bunch, Marley or Archer.

Most papers carried the story as a one- or two-sentence telegraphic brief, under headings such as "Lynching in Indiana" in the Sacramento Daily Record-Union and Memphis Daily Appeal and "Judge Lynch" in the Tombstone Weekly Epitaph. The Salt Lake Herald filed it under "Criminalities," the Cheyenne Daily Leader among its "Telegraphic Ticks," and the Illinois Staats-Zeitung in a German-language weekly crime roundup. Transmission garbled the names into Bundy, Bandy, Randy and Paelo, and Marley into Morley and Murley.

The syndicated paragraph that ran in the Batesville Guard and other Southern weeklies in early August led with the brutality of Archer's murder before reporting the hanging. The Paoli News took a different line, calling the situation "a deplorable state of affairs," noting that its account was gathered "from the many reports in circulation," and expressing hope that the suspicion would prove unfounded.

Accounts differ on the victim's name, his fate and the date. The Paoli News named him Anderson Bunch and described only a disappearance on July 11, while the wire reports named him Bundy and reported a completed hanging. The Daily Gazette dated the lynching to the night of July 15, the New Albany dispatch gave July 15 as the date of Archer's murder, and the Daily Kennebec Journal said "Tuesday night." As the local paper closest to the events, the Paoli News is the more direct source, though it too relied on rumor.

bases: Wire dispatches report that a mob hanged a man named Bundy for aiding a murderer's escape (A4, A6, A16), though the local Paoli News treated his death as an unconfirmed suspicion (A13).

Wire reports say a mob hanged Bundy and threw his body into Lost River as punishment for aiding Archer's murderer to escape (A4, A6, A16), but the only local account, from the Paoli News, says only that Anderson Bunch was missing, that pistol shots were heard, and that searchers were dragging the river, and hoped the suspicion would prove unfounded (A13); no report of a body being found appears.

The wire reports (A2-A7, A9, A11, A16) appear to stem from a single New Albany dispatch and state a lynching as fact, while the local Paoli News reprint (A13) describes only a disappearance and suspected foul play.

accounts.label: New Albany wire dispatch
accounts.gist: News from Paoli said Bundy, who had sheltered Archer's murderer Marley and aided his escape, was hanged at night by a mob and his body thrown into Lost River.

accounts.label: Paoli News (local)
accounts.gist: Anderson Bunch, reported friendly to Marley, had been missing since July 11; pistol shots were heard near where he was last seen, and searchers were dragging Lost River, but the editor called this rumor and hoped the suspicion unfounded.

accounts.label: Syndicated paragraph
accounts.gist: Marley murdered Archer at West Baden Springs 'in a most cowardly and brutal manner'; a mob captured Bundy, hanged him to a tree and threw his body in the river.

framing.detail: Most papers ran one- or two-sentence briefs under 'Lynching in Indiana', 'Judge Lynch' or 'Criminalities', stating the lynching as fact and naming Bundy's 'crime' as aiding the escape.

The Paoli News, reprinted in the Jasper Weekly Courier, treated the case as a suspected revenge murder built on 'the many reports in circulation' and warned of 'erroneous opinions and wrong suspicions'.
A later syndicated paragraph stressed Archer's 'cowardly and brutal' murder before reporting the mob hanging.
